title: the DSG mining products of a mine

banner.title: The DSG MINING PRODUCTS OF A MINE, R521: printed p. 50 (pdf 51) - the products rules: when a miner successfully locates minerals the player rolls 1d100 on Table 30 Mining Products (the nine bands - copper 01-30, tin 31-40, lead 41-66, iron 67-84, silver 85-92, gold 93-97, platinum 98, mithril 99, gemstones 00), the mithril possibility (the material needed for elven chain mail, a mithril mine only deep under the earth in the most solid of bedrock - if the locale qualifies the player rolls 1d10 on Table 31 Mithril Check, otherwise reroll on Table 30; Table 31 gives silver, gold and platinum at highest quality on 1-5/6-8/9 and mithril on 10), and the gemstone determination on Table 32 (sixteen stone types in d100 bands from bloodstone 01-08 and onyx 09-18 through emerald 93-96, with 97-99 rolling twice and 00 rolling three times - the 97-or-greater result grants its additional rolls immediately and any additional 97+ grants them again with no limit, a duplicated substance is noted as Jade x2 and yields twice the usual amount, and one quality level applies to all stones of a single type in a mine)
banner.provenance: the DSG scan (archive.org item advanced-dungeons-dragons-1st-edition), pdf = printed + 1; the text read from the IA djvu OCR (djvu.txt lines ~6588-6650) with the pdf Acrobat-Capture layer as the second read (idx 119-121 = printed pp. 49-51 window) and the compiled-tables appendix reprint as the third read. THE BLOODSTONE READ: the Table 32 01-08 row is the garble of the round - the djvu drops the row entirely (the table jumps from the header to 09-18 onyx), the Capture layer renders it as a "-1/^^" fragment, and the appendix reprint drops it too; all three machine reads fail the row, and it was settled as BLOODSTONE (01-08) by Curtiss reading the physical printed page 50 - the physical read outranks the scan. Everything else multi-confirms: the Table 30 nine bands (djvu clean, Capture corroborating iron 67-84 through gold 93-97, the appendix reprint corroborating the full ladder), the Table 31 four bands (djvu, Capture and appendix all agree on 1-5/6-8/9/10 with the highest-quality silver/gold/platinum), and the Table 32 bands from 09-18 onyx through 00 (djvu and Capture agree; the appendix adds the 55-60 amethyst row the chapter djvu dropped). The 1d10 mithril check pins as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention (the djvu "1410" and Capture "ldlO" garbles both read as 1d10). The 00 band pins as roll 100. The Tables 33-34 quality grids start the NEXT round per the content-density rule.
banner.sentinel: Three tables pin: Table 30 as a 9x2 d100 band grid (the 00 gemstones band pinned as roll 100), Table 31 as a 4x2 d10 band grid, and Table 32 as an 18x2 d100 band grid (sixteen stone types plus the roll-twice and roll-three-times bands, the 00 band as 100). The 1d100 products roll and the 1d10 mithril check pin as dice + sides consts per the R508 convention. The 97-or-greater extra-roll threshold pins as a const; the unlimited recursion, the duplicate doubling and the one-quality-per-type rules pin as prose bools. The 01-08 bloodstone row pins from the physical book read (the standing physical-outranks-scan lesson). The R518/R520 seams (DMG 106 rates, DSG 53 duration) are noted; nothing auto-credits.

consts.name: dnprT30RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 30 mining products grid carries nine d100 bands (the 00 gemstones band pinned as roll 100).

consts.name: dnprT30Dice
consts.comment: the products roll is one die.

consts.name: dnprT30Sides
consts.comment: the products roll is 1d100 when a miner successfully locates minerals.

consts.name: dnprMithrilCheckDice
consts.comment: the mithril check roll is one die.

consts.name: dnprMithrilCheckSides
consts.comment: the mithril check roll is 1d10 compared to Table 31 (the djvu "1410" and Capture "ldlO" garbles both read as 1d10).

consts.name: dnprT31RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 31 mithril check grid carries the four d10 bands.

consts.name: dnprT32RowCount
consts.comment: the Table 32 gemstones grid carries eighteen d100 bands (sixteen stone types plus the roll-twice and roll-three-times bands).

consts.name: dnprT32ExtraRollThreshold
consts.comment: a roll of 97 or greater on Table 32 immediately grants the additional rolls indicated.

bools.name: dnprRollT30OnLocatingMinerals
bools.comment: when a miner successfully locates minerals, the player rolls 1d100 and finds the result on Table 30: Mining Products.

bools.name: dnprMithrilForElvenChainMail
bools.comment: the Table 30 mithril entry is the possibility of mithril, the material needed to create elven chain mail.

bools.name: dnprMithrilOnlyDeepSolidBedrock
bools.comment: a mithril mine can only exist deep under the earth in the most solid of bedrock.

bools.name: dnprMithrilElseRerollT30
bools.comment: if the locale of the mine is in such an area, the player rolls 1d10 against Table 31: Mithril Check; otherwise, reroll on the Mining Products table.

bools.name: dnprT31MetalsHighestQuality
bools.comment: the Table 31 silver, gold and platinum results are the highest quality of their metal.

bools.name: dnprT32ExtraRollsImmediate
bools.comment: if a 97 or greater is rolled on Table 32, the player immediately makes the additional rolls indicated.

bools.name: dnprT32ExtraRollsNoLimit
bools.comment: any additional roll that again yields 97 or better grants its additional rolls - there is no limit to the number of rolls possible.

bools.name: dnprT32DuplicateDoublesYield
bools.comment: a result yielding the same substance twice is noted (e.g., Jade x2) - the mine yields twice the usual amount of that mineral.

bools.name: dnprT32OneQualityPerType
bools.comment: the same level of quality applies to all of a single type of stone found in a mine.
